answer: Each agent may open a work channel only after locking a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when independent audits show it copied another identity’s behavior. Auditors sample actions across time, so splitting one operator across velvet, ridge, and horizon channels does not create independent histories; correlated responses expose the cluster. The attacker must fund every identity up front and risks losing those funds, making mass fabrication costly rather than merely a matter of generating more keys.
